thread.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Alphabet (GOOGL) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Google earnings (Shutterstock photo)
Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) is set to report fourth quarter fiscal 2017 earnings results Thursday after the closing bell. And depending on how investors respond to the numbers, the tech giant may once-again surpass Apple ( AAPL ) as the world’s most valuable company.
Google shares have opened 2018 on a strong note, climbing 12% year to date, compared with a 5.5% rise for the S&P 500 Index. Those gains, which yielded an all-time high of $1,198 on Monday, has pushed the company’s market cap north of $800 billion to around $812 billion, putting it only an eyelash away from Apple’s market cap of $850 billion.
The company’s dominance in the digital ad industry, where it competes with Facebook ( FB ), remains a driving force. And there’s no sign of slowing down, given the industry’s growth forecast for the next three years.
“Digital spending will see double-digit growth each year, soaring from $83.00 billion in 2017 to $129.23 billion in 2021,” according to market research firm eMarketer. These trends bode well for what Google might be able to do in the quarters and years ahead.
Thanks to its widely-visited online assets such as YouTube, Google is well-positioned to capture a sizable portion of those ad revenues. For now, all eyes will focus on this quarter, particularly as advertisers tend to ramp up spending to secure more holiday shopping dollars. The expected surge in spending should reflect handsomely on both the top and bottom lines.
In the period that ended December, Wall Street is looking for the Mountain View, Calif.-based tech giant to deliver adjusted earnings of $9.98 per share on revenue of $31.87 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $9.36 per share on revenue of $26.06 billion. For the full year, earnings of $32.31 per share would be down from $34.34 a year ago, while full-year revenue of the $110.4 billion would rise 22.3% year over year.
In the third quarter, the company’s advertising business grew 23% year over year to $24.1 billion and contributed to almost 90% of revenue. On Thursday analysts will dig deep into those metrics to assess the overall health of the segment. In Q3, while aggregate paid clicks grew 47% year over year and 6% sequentially, aggregate cost-per-click fell 18% year over year.
The cost-per-click metric is closely-watched because it is the price advertisers pay every time a user clicks on their online advertisements. Investors would love to see an improvement Thursday. Analysts will also look to see how the company’s Other Bets segments, which focuses on areas such as self-driving cars, artificial intelligence and smartphones, performs.
The company’s cloud computing capabilities, where it competes with Amazon’s ( AMZN ) dominant AWS cloud platform and Microsoft’s ( MSFT ) Azure, will also be an important topic.
Assuming Google is able to deliver a top and bottom-line beat, solid cost-per-click performance and issue confident guidance, the tech conglomerate would have done enough to send its shares higher. As to whether it passes Apple as the world’s most valuable company, that will depend on what Apple, which also reports results Thursday, is able to do.
